meta.title: Level crossings, motorways and residential zones
meta.summary: You will learn when you must not enter a level crossing and what to do if your car gets stuck on the tracks, what is prohibited on a motorway, and how to behave in a residential zone and in a yard.

p: You may cross railway tracks only at a level crossing, giving way to a train, locomotive or draisine. A train cannot turn aside or stop quickly: its braking distance is measured in hundreds of metres.

As you approach a level crossing, watch the signs, the traffic light, the road markings, the position of the barrier and the attendant's instructions. And in any case, make sure yourself that there is no train.

lesson.h: Traffic light signals at a level crossing
p: A flashing red signal, like any red signal, prohibits movement. An audible signal may sound with it, which also signals the prohibition.
A flashing lunar white signal permits movement over the crossing. If both the red and the lunar white signals are off, you may go only after making sure that no train is approaching the crossing.

A permitting signal does not remove the need to check the tracks: if a train is approaching the crossing, you must not enter it. And if the level crossing attendant gives a prohibiting signal, obey it even when the traffic light permits movement.
lesson.tip: A flashing red signal at a level crossing prohibits entry even if the barrier is raised or there is no barrier at all.

lesson.h: When you must not enter a level crossing
list: The barrier is closed or beginning to close - regardless of the traffic light signal.
The traffic light shows a prohibiting signal - regardless of whether there is a barrier and what position it is in.
The attendant gives a prohibiting signal: they stand with their chest or back towards you, holding up a baton, a red lamp or a flag, or with their arms extended to the sides.
There is a traffic jam beyond the crossing that would force you to stop on the tracks.
A train, locomotive or draisine is approaching the crossing within sight.
lesson.tip: If there is a traffic jam beyond the crossing, wait before it, even when the traffic light permits movement.

lesson.h: What else is prohibited at a level crossing
list: Crossing the tracks anywhere except at a level crossing.
Driving around vehicles stopped before the crossing by moving into the oncoming lane.
Opening the barrier without authorisation.

Moving agricultural, road-building or construction machinery in a non-transport configuration, as well as slow-moving vehicles travelling at less than 8 km/h and tractor-drawn sledges, across the crossing without permission from the head of the track section.
Overtaking on the crossing and within 100 m before it, making a U-turn or reversing on the crossing, stopping on the crossing itself, and parking within 50 m of it.

lesson.h: Where to stop if you must not go on
p: Stop at the stop line, sign 2.5 “No passing without stopping (Stop)”, or the traffic light. If none of these are present, stop at the boundary of the level crossing. The boundary of the crossing is an imaginary line 10 m from the nearest rail.
Sign 2.5 before a level crossing always requires you to stop, even if there is no train: at the stop line or, if there is none, before the sign.

lesson.h: If your car stalls on the crossing
list: Immediately get everyone out of the car and take steps to clear the crossing.

If possible, send two people along the tracks in both directions for 1000 m. If there is only one person, send them in the direction where the track is less visible. Explain to them how to give the train driver a stop signal.
Stay by the car yourself and give general alarm signals.
When a train appears, run towards it, giving the stop signal.
lesson.tip: The stop signal is a circular movement of the arm (by day with a bright piece of cloth or another conspicuous object, by night with a flare or a lamp). The general alarm signal is a series of one long and three short sound signals.

p: A motorway (sign 5.1) is designed for fast traffic, so anything that suddenly slows the flow down is prohibited here. A passenger car travels there at the speed shown on sign 3.24, but not more than 140 km/h.
list: Pedestrians and domestic animals being outside a vehicle, and riding bicycles, mopeds, tractors, self-propelled machines or other vehicles whose speed, by technical specification or condition, is below 40 km/h.
Trucks over 3.5 t travelling beyond the second lane.
Stopping anywhere other than special parking areas marked with sign 5.15 “Parking place” or sign 6.11 “Rest area”.
Making a U-turn and entering service gaps in the central reservation.
Reversing.
Learner driving.
lesson.tip: Missed your exit - drive on to the next one. Reversing and making a U-turn are prohibited on a motorway.

lesson.h: A forced stop on a motorway
p: If your car comes to a forced stop on the carriageway, mark it out: switch on the hazard warning lights and put out the warning triangle. Then try to move it onto the strip to the right of the line marking the edge of the carriageway.
All these rules also apply on roads marked with sign 5.3 “Road for motor vehicles”. This road is for motor cars and motorcycles only.

lesson.h: Residential zone: the pedestrian is in charge here
p: A residential zone is marked with sign 5.38 “Residential zone”. Pedestrians may walk both on the pavement and on the carriageway, and they have priority. But they must not obstruct vehicles without reason either.
The speed in a residential zone and in yards is no more than 20 km/h. A child may suddenly run out from behind a parked car, so the driver must be ready to stop at any moment.

lesson.h: What is prohibited in a residential zone and how to leave it
list: Through traffic, that is, driving through a residential zone to cut your route short.
Driving off the carriageway.
Learner driving.
Parking with the engine running (an exception is made for electric cars).
Parking trucks over 3.5 t and buses outside specially marked places.
Sounding the horn and playing loud music.
Parking on pavements, lawns, or children's and sports playgrounds.
lesson.tip: When leaving a residential zone or a yard, you give way to everyone. The same rules apply in residential courtyards.

keyFacts: You may cross railway tracks only at a level crossing, giving way to a train ⟦1⟧

You must not enter a level crossing when the barrier is closed or beginning to close, regardless of the traffic light, or when the traffic light shows a prohibiting signal, regardless of the barrier ⟦2⟧
You must not enter a level crossing if there is a traffic jam beyond it that would force you to stop on the tracks ⟦3⟧
Slow-moving vehicles travelling at less than 8 km/h may cross a level crossing only with permission from the head of the track section ⟦4⟧
If you must not go on, stop at the stop line, sign 2.5 or the traffic light, or, if none of these are present, at the boundary of the crossing ⟦5⟧
If you get stuck on a level crossing: get everyone out of the car, clear the crossing, and if possible send two people along the tracks in both directions for 1000 m ⟦6⟧
The general alarm signal is one long and three short sound signals; the stop signal to a train is a circular movement of the arm ⟦7⟧
On a motorway, U-turns, entering service gaps in the central reservation, reversing and learner driving are prohibited ⟦8⟧
Pedestrians, bicycles, mopeds, tractors and vehicles whose speed, by specification or condition, is below 40 km/h are not allowed on a motorway ⟦9⟧
You may stop on a motorway only at areas marked with sign 5.15 or 6.11 ⟦10⟧
In a residential zone, the pedestrian has priority, and the speed is limited to 20 km/h ⟦11⟧
When leaving a residential zone, the driver gives way to everyone; the rules for a residential zone also apply in yards ⟦12⟧
mistakes: Trying to dash through while the barrier is still coming down. Entry is already prohibited once the barrier starts to close.
Entering a level crossing behind a queue of traffic. If there is a jam beyond the crossing, wait before it, or you risk being stranded on the tracks.
Driving around a queue before a level crossing using the oncoming lane. This is separately prohibited.
Reversing back to a missed exit on a motorway. Reversing and making a U-turn are prohibited there.
Sounding the horn at a pedestrian in a residential zone to make them move out of the way. There, the pedestrian has priority, and using the horn is prohibited.
Relying on the “priority to the right” rule when leaving a yard. When leaving a residential zone or a yard, you give way to everyone.

questions.q: You are approaching a level crossing. The traffic light has not come on yet, but the barrier has started to come down. What should you do?
options: Try to get through before the barrier closes completely
Stop before the crossing
Drive on if there is no train visible in either direction
Drive on: the traffic light does not yet prohibit anything
questions.explain: Entering a level crossing is prohibited when the barrier is closed or beginning to close, regardless of the traffic light signal.

questions.q: What do the Rules call a level crossing?
options: An intersection of a road with railway tracks at the same level
Any bridge or tunnel where a road passes over or under the tracks
A stretch of road 100 m before the railway tracks
Only a place with a barrier and a traffic light by the tracks
questions.explain: A level crossing is an intersection of a road with railway tracks at the same level. Its boundary is an imaginary line 10 m from the nearest rail. A level crossing may have no barrier and no traffic light at all.

questions.q: The level crossing attendant is standing with their back to you, arms extended to the sides. May you drive across the crossing?
options: No: this is a prohibiting signal
Yes: the attendant is standing with their back to you
Yes, if there is no train in sight
Yes, but only at low speed
questions.explain: The attendant's prohibiting signal: they face the driver with their chest or back while holding up a baton, a red lamp or a flag, or they stand with their arms extended to the sides.

questions.q: There is a queue of vehicles before a closed level crossing, and the oncoming lane is clear. What do you do?
options: Drive around the queue using the oncoming lane and take first place
Join the queue behind the last vehicle
Sound the horn so the queue moves over to the right
questions.explain: It is prohibited to drive around vehicles stopped before a level crossing by moving into the oncoming lane.

questions.q: Your car has stalled right on a level crossing, with passengers inside. What must you do first?
options: Stay in the car with the passengers and call a tow truck
Switch on the hazard warning lights and wait for the level crossing attendant
Keep trying to start the engine until it works
Immediately get everyone out of the car and clear the crossing
questions.explain: At a forced stop on a level crossing, the driver must immediately get everyone out of the car and take steps to clear the crossing.

questions.q: You are stuck on a level crossing and cannot clear it yet. You have two passengers with you. How do the Rules say you should use their help?
options: Send them along the tracks in both directions from the crossing for 1000 m
Send both of them 100 m in the direction of better visibility
Send them along the tracks in both directions for 300 m
Ask them to stay in the car and call the police
questions.explain: If possible, you should send two people along the tracks in both directions from the crossing for 1000 m (if there is only one person, in the direction of worse visibility of the track) and explain to them how to give the train driver a stop signal.

questions.q: You have been driving on a motorway for a long time and want to rest. Where may you stop?
options: On the shoulder anywhere, having switched on the hazard warning lights
In the right-hand lane, having put out the warning triangle
At a parking area marked with sign 5.15 or 6.11
In a service gap in the central reservation
questions.explain: On a motorway, stopping anywhere other than special parking areas marked with sign 5.15 or 6.11 is prohibited.

questions.q: A moped is riding ahead of you on a road marked with sign 5.3 “Road for motor vehicles”. Is it allowed to be there?
options: Yes, if it keeps to the far right edge of the road
No: mopeds are not allowed on such a road
Yes, if the moped has its headlight on
Yes, but only during daylight hours
questions.explain: Sign 5.3 marks a road for motor cars and motorcycles only, and the rules for motorways apply on it. Riding mopeds, bicycles or tractors there is prohibited.

questions.q: On a motorway, your tyre has gone flat and your car has stopped on the carriageway. What must you do?
options: Leave the car in the lane and walk off to get help
Mark the car and move it beyond the edge of the carriageway
Switch on the hazard warning lights and reverse to the exit
Put out the warning triangle and change the tyre right there in your lane
questions.explain: At a forced stop on the carriageway, the driver marks the car under the rules of Chapter 7: switches on the hazard warning lights and puts out the warning triangle. Then the driver takes steps to move the car onto the strip to the right of the line marking the edge of the carriageway.

questions.q: Because of a gearbox fault, your car cannot go faster than 35 km/h. May you drive it onto a motorway?
options: Yes, if you keep to the right-hand lane with the hazard warning lights on
Yes, if you drive on the shoulder and do not obstruct the traffic flow
Yes, but only during daylight hours
No: its speed is below 40 km/h
questions.explain: On motorways, vehicles whose speed, by technical specification or condition, is below 40 km/h are prohibited from travelling.

questions.q: You have arrived in the yard of an apartment block, and all the places by the edge of the driveway are taken. May you park on the lawn by the entrance?
options: Yes, if the car does not obstruct pedestrians
Yes, if only the right-hand wheels are on the lawn
Yes, at night, when there are no children in the yard
No: parking on lawns in yards is prohibited
questions.explain: The rules for a residential zone also apply in residential courtyards. Parking there is prohibited on pavements, lawns, or children's and sports playgrounds, even if the car is not in anyone's way.

questions.q: There is a traffic jam on the street, and you want to cut your route short by driving straight through a residential zone. May you do this?
options: Yes, if you do not exceed 20 km/h
Yes, but only during daytime hours
No: through traffic there is prohibited
Yes, if you do not sound the horn on the way
questions.explain: Through traffic is prohibited in a residential zone.

questions.q: You are entering the yard of a residential building, and there is no “Residential zone” sign. What is the highest speed you may drive here?
options: 20 km/h
30 km/h
40 km/h
60 km/h
questions.explain: The 20 km/h limit applies both in residential zones and in residential courtyards. The other requirements of the residential zone chapter also extend to yards.

questions.q: At a level crossing without a barrier, the red traffic light signals are flashing. There is no train in sight either to the left or to the right. What should you do?
options: Drive on: without a barrier, the red signal is only a warning
Drive on slowly, having looked both ways once more
Stop at the stop line and wait until the red signals go off
Drive on, sounding a long blast of the horn
questions.explain: A red signal, including a flashing one, prohibits movement. You must not enter a level crossing when the traffic light shows a prohibiting signal, regardless of whether there is a barrier or what position it is in, even if no train is visible yet.

questions.q: The barrier is closed, but the traffic light at the crossing is off, and there is no train in sight. May you drive across?
options: Yes, if there is no train visible in either direction
You may drive around the barrier using the oncoming lane
No: entry is prohibited when the barrier is closed
Yes, if the traffic light has not come on for several minutes
questions.explain: Entering a level crossing when the barrier is closed or beginning to close is prohibited, whatever the traffic light shows. Driving around the barrier is even less permitted.

questions.q: At a level crossing without a barrier, a lunar white signal is flashing. What should you do?
options: Drive across the crossing after making sure no train is approaching
Stop: any flashing signal at a level crossing prohibits movement
Stop and wait for the level crossing attendant
questions.explain: A flashing lunar white signal at a level crossing permits movement. But even so, the driver must make sure that no train is approaching the crossing.

questions.q: A passenger asks you to stop right on the level crossing so they can get out quickly. There is no train in sight. May you do this?
options: Yes, if the stop takes less than a minute
No: stopping on a level crossing is prohibited
Yes, if you switch on the hazard warning lights
Yes, if the barrier is up and the traffic light is off
questions.explain: Stopping on level crossings is prohibited in any case, even for a minute and even when there is no train in sight. Drop the passenger off beyond the crossing, where stopping is allowed.

questions.q: The traffic light at the crossing is off, there is no barrier, and a train is approaching the crossing from the left. What should you do?
options: Drive across quickly before the train arrives
Sound the horn and drive across
Drive across: the traffic light is off, so movement is permitted
Stop before the crossing and let the train pass
questions.explain: Entering a level crossing is prohibited if a train is approaching it within sight, even when the traffic light is off and there is no barrier. A train cannot turn aside or stop quickly.

questions.q: The traffic light permits movement, but there are vehicles standing right beyond the crossing, and there is no room for you beyond the tracks. May you enter the crossing?
options: Yes: the traffic light permits movement, and the barrier is up
No, as long as there is no room for you beyond the crossing
Yes, if you switch on the hazard warning lights
Yes, if you stop right at the edge of the crossing
questions.explain: Entering a level crossing is prohibited if a jam has formed beyond it that would force you to stop on the tracks. Wait before the crossing until room clears beyond it.

questions.q: A lunar white signal is flashing at the crossing, but the level crossing attendant is facing you with arms extended to the sides. What should you do?
options: Drive on: the lunar white signal permits movement
Stop: the attendant's signal prohibits entering the crossing
Drive on slowly if there is no train in sight
Drive on, sounding the horn at the attendant
questions.explain: The level crossing attendant is a traffic controller, and a traffic controller's signals must be obeyed even if they contradict the traffic light. An attendant facing the driver with arms extended to the sides is prohibiting entry to the crossing.

questions.q: The level crossing attendant is facing you and has raised an arm holding a baton. May you enter the crossing?
options: Yes, if the barrier is open and the traffic light is off
Yes, if there is no train visible in either direction
Yes, but only at low speed
No: this is the attendant's prohibiting signal
questions.explain: An attendant facing the driver with their chest or back, holding up a baton, a red lamp or a flag, is prohibiting entry to the crossing. An open barrier does not cancel this.

questions.q: The barrier is closed. Where must you stop?
options: At the stop line
Right up against the barrier
At the nearest rail
50 m before the crossing
questions.explain: When movement across a level crossing is prohibited, the driver stops at the stop line, sign 2.5 or the traffic light. Here there is a stop line.

questions.q: There is no stop line, sign 2.5 or traffic light here. A train is approaching the crossing. Where must you stop?
options: Right at the rail, so you can drive across faster afterwards
3 m from the nearest rail, at the edge of the decking
100 m from the crossing, right at the warning sign
At the boundary of the crossing, 10 m from the nearest rail
questions.explain: If there is no stop line, sign 2.5 or traffic light, the driver stops at the boundary of the crossing. It runs along an imaginary line 10 m from the nearest rail.

questions.q: Sign 2.5 is installed before the crossing, and there is no stop line. There is no train in sight. What should you do?
options: Drive across without stopping: there is no train in sight, and no traffic light either
Stop before the sign, then drive on if there is no train
Stop right at the rail and look both ways
Slow down to 20 km/h and drive across without stopping
questions.explain: Sign 2.5 before a level crossing requires you to stop in any case: before the stop line, or, if there is none, before the sign. Then, after making sure there is no train, you may go on.

questions.q: Your car has stalled on the crossing, and you cannot clear it yet. You have one passenger with you. Where should you send them?
options: Along the tracks for 100 m, in the direction where the track is more visible
Along the tracks for 1000 m, in the direction where the track is less visible
To the nearest house to call for help
Nowhere: let them stay in the car and wait
questions.explain: Everyone must be got out of the car straight away. If only one person can help, they are sent along the tracks for 1000 m in the direction of worse visibility, and told how to give the train driver a stop signal.

questions.q: You have not managed to clear the crossing, and a train has appeared in the distance. What must you do?
options: Get into the car and try to start the engine again
Move away from the crossing and wait
Stay by the car and flash the headlights
Run towards the train, giving the driver the stop signal
questions.explain: When a train appears, the driver runs towards it and gives the stop signal: circular movements of the arm, by day with a bright piece of cloth or a clearly visible object, by night with a flare or a lamp.

questions.q: Your car is stuck on the crossing. You have got the passengers out and sent two people along the tracks. What do you do yourself?
options: Go to the nearest house to call for help
Wait inside the car with my seat belt on
Also go off along the tracks to look for help
Stay by the car and give general alarm signals
questions.explain: The driver stays by the car and gives general alarm signals: a series of one long and three short sound signals. When a train appears, the driver runs towards it giving the stop signal.

questions.q: You are driving a slow-moving tractor with a top speed of 6 km/h. May you cross this level crossing on your own?
options: Yes, if there is no train visible in either direction
Yes, if you switch on an amber beacon
Yes, if the level crossing attendant does not object
Not without permission from the head of the track section
questions.explain: A slow-moving vehicle stays on the tracks for a long time. That is why crossing a level crossing with a vehicle travelling at less than 8 km/h is prohibited without permission from the head of the track section.

questions.q: The barrier has been closed for 15 minutes already, the traffic light is off, and there is no train in sight. May you raise the barrier yourself and drive across?
options: Yes, if there is no train visible in either direction
No: opening the barrier without authorisation is prohibited
Yes, if there is no level crossing attendant nearby
Yes, if you lower the barrier again straight after crossing
questions.explain: Opening the barrier at a level crossing without authorisation is prohibited, and you must not enter the crossing while the barrier is closed. You must wait for it to be raised.

questions.q: The nearest level crossing is 3 km away, and there is a worn track leading across the rails nearby. May you cross the railway there?
options: Yes, if there is no train visible in either direction
Yes, but only in daylight and at low speed
No: you may cross the tracks only at a level crossing
Yes, if the track is well worn and even
questions.explain: Drivers may cross railway tracks only at a level crossing. Crossing the tracks elsewhere is prohibited: there is neither signalling nor a level surface there.

questions.q: You have entered the crossing and realised you turned the wrong way. May you make a U-turn right on the crossing or reverse?
options: You may make a U-turn if there is no train in sight
You may only reverse if there is no one behind you
No: both a U-turn and reversing are prohibited here
You may do either with the hazard warning lights on
questions.explain: Making a U-turn on level crossings is prohibited, and reversing is not allowed anywhere a U-turn is prohibited. Drive across the crossing and make your U-turn further on, at a permitted place.

questions.q: There is a traffic jam ahead on the motorway. May you make a U-turn through the gap in the central reservation, as shown?
options: Yes, if the oncoming lane beyond the gap is clear
Yes, if you switch on the hazard warning lights
No: this is prohibited on a motorway
Yes, if the jam has lasted more than 15 minutes
questions.explain: Vehicles travel fast on a motorway, and a U-turn across the flow of traffic is very dangerous. That is why both making a U-turn and entering service gaps in the central reservation are prohibited there. Wait for the nearest exit.

questions.q: You have driven 50 m past the exit you needed. May you go back to it by reversing along the shoulder?
options: Yes, if you switch on the hazard warning lights
Yes, if there is no one behind you on the shoulder
Yes, if the missed exit is less than 100 m away
No: reversing on a motorway is prohibited
questions.explain: Reversing on a motorway is prohibited, including along the shoulder. Drive on to the next exit.

questions.q: You are driving a truck with a maximum authorised mass of 12 t. May you travel in this lane on the motorway?
options: Yes, if this lane is currently free of other vehicles
Yes, but only to overtake other trucks
No: you are not allowed to travel beyond the second lane
Yes, if you do not exceed 90 km/h
questions.explain: You are travelling in the third lane. On a motorway, trucks with a maximum authorised mass over 3.5 t are prohibited from travelling beyond the second lane, even to overtake.

questions.q: You are driving a truck with a maximum authorised mass of 12 t. May you overtake another truck using the second lane, as shown?
options: Yes: the ban applies only beyond the second lane
No: trucks are allowed only the far right lane
Yes, but only at a speed of no more than 60 km/h
questions.explain: The prohibition for trucks over 3.5 t on a motorway applies to lanes beyond the second. The second lane may be used, including for overtaking.

questions.q: A passenger asks you to drop them off on the shoulder of the motorway so they can continue on foot. May you do this?
options: Yes, if you switch on the hazard warning lights and put out the warning triangle
No: both that kind of stop and pedestrians are prohibited there
Yes, if they walk along the shoulder facing the oncoming traffic
Yes, if you drop them off beyond the line marking the edge of the carriageway
questions.explain: Two prohibitions are broken here at once. Pedestrians are not allowed on a motorway, and stopping is allowed only at areas marked with sign 5.15 or 6.11.

questions.q: A tractor is travelling ahead of you on the motorway. Is it allowed to be there?
options: Yes, if it keeps to the far right lane
No: tractors are prohibited from driving here
Yes, if it has an amber beacon switched on
Yes, if it travels at no less than 30 km/h
questions.explain: Tractors, self-propelled machines, mopeds, bicycles and other vehicles that cannot travel faster than 40 km/h are prohibited on a motorway. A slow vehicle among fast-moving traffic is very dangerous.

questions.q: An instructor suggests that a learner practise driving at high speed on a motorway. May they do this?
options: Yes, if the car is fitted with dual controls
Yes, during daylight hours and in dry weather
Yes, if they keep to the right-hand lane
No: learner driving is prohibited here
questions.explain: Learner driving is prohibited on motorways, even with an instructor. The high speed of the traffic leaves a beginner no time for a mistake.

questions.q: You are driving on a road with sign 5.3 and have missed the turning you needed. May you make a U-turn, as shown?
options: Yes: the road markings are broken, so crossing them is allowed
No: the prohibitions for a motorway apply here
Yes, if there are no oncoming vehicles nearby
questions.explain: Sign 5.3 marks a road for motor vehicles. The requirements of the chapter on motorways also extend to such roads, so making a U-turn here is prohibited, whatever the road markings are.

questions.q: You are driving in a residential zone, and children are playing on the carriageway. What should you do?
options: Sound the horn so the children move away
Drive around the children on the pavement, since it is clear
Drive between the children without slowing down
Slow down and let the children pass
questions.explain: In a residential zone, pedestrians may be on the carriageway and have priority. Sounding the horn is prohibited there, and driving off the carriageway is not allowed.

questions.q: In a residential zone, you have stopped by the edge of the driveway and have been talking on the phone for 15 minutes without switching off your petrol engine, to keep the air conditioning running. May you do this?
options: Yes, if none of the residents complain about the noise
Yes, if you switch on the hazard warning lights
No: parking with the engine running is prohibited here
Yes, if you do not stand for more than half an hour
questions.explain: You have been standing for more than 5 minutes, not to pick up passengers or load goods, so this is parking. Parking with the engine running is prohibited in a residential zone; an exception is made only for electric cars.

questions.q: You are turning right as you leave a residential zone. Who must you give way to?
options: Only the white car
Only the pedestrian
Both
Neither
questions.explain: When leaving a residential zone, the driver gives way to all other road users. First let the pedestrian walking on the pavement pass, and the white car on the street.

questions.q: A white car is pulling out of a yard. Which of you goes first?
options: You
The white car
Whoever arrived first
questions.explain: The rules for a residential zone also apply in residential courtyards. A driver leaving a yard gives way to everyone, so you go first.

questions.q: In a residential zone, the driveway is narrowed by a parked car. May you drive around it by putting your wheels on the pavement?
options: No: driving off the carriageway is prohibited here
Yes, if there are no pedestrians on the pavement right now
Yes, if you drive on the pavement at no more than 5 km/h
Yes, if only your right-hand wheels go onto the pavement
questions.explain: Driving vehicles off the carriageway is prohibited in a residential zone. The pavement is meant for pedestrians, even if there is no one on it right now.

questions.q: Which of the drivers is allowed to stop on the motorway?
options: Only the blue car
Both
Neither
Only the red car
questions.explain: On a motorway, you may stop only at special parking areas marked with sign 5.15 or 6.11. The red car has pulled into such an area, while the blue car has stopped on the shoulder.

questions.q: A truck with a maximum authorised mass of 8 t and a blue car have been standing in a residential zone for more than an hour. There are no special parking places here. Who is allowed to park like this?
options: Only the 8 t truck
Both
Neither
Only the blue car
questions.explain: Parking trucks with a maximum authorised mass over 3.5 t and buses outside specially designated and marked places is prohibited in a residential zone. The blue car is allowed to park by the edge.

questions.q: Who is allowed to park in the residential zone?
options: Only the red car
Only the blue car
Both
Neither
questions.explain: Parking on pavements is prohibited in a residential zone, even if the car does not obstruct pedestrians. The blue car has pulled onto the pavement, while the red car is standing by the edge of the carriageway.

questions.q: A bus is parked at a place marked with sign 5.15, and a truck with a maximum authorised mass of 8 t is by the edge of the carriageway. Who is allowed to park in the residential zone?
options: Only the bus
Only the truck
Both
Neither
questions.explain: Buses and trucks over 3.5 t may park in a residential zone only at specially designated places marked with signs or road markings. The bus is at a place marked with sign 5.15, but the truck is not.

questions.q: A truck with a maximum authorised mass of 8 t has been unloading furniture for 15 minutes, and a bus has been standing here for an hour already. There are no special parking places. Who is this allowed to?
options: Only the truck
Only the parked bus
Both
Neither
questions.explain: Unloading counts as stopping, and in a residential zone only parking outside special places is prohibited for trucks. The bus has been standing for an hour, which is parking, and outside marked places this is prohibited for it.

questions.q: In a residential zone, two cars have been standing with their engines running for 20 minutes: an electric car and a petrol car. Who is this allowed to?
options: Only the electric car
Only the petrol car
Both
Neither
questions.explain: Parking with the engine running is prohibited in a residential zone. An exception is made only for the electric car.

questions.q: Who must a driver give way to at a level crossing?
options: Only a passenger train
A train, locomotive or draisine
No one, if the traffic light is off
Oncoming vehicles
questions.explain: Railway tracks are crossed at level crossings, giving way to a train, locomotive or draisine. They cannot turn aside and take hundreds of metres to stop.

questions.q: Outside town, a field track runs up to the railway tracks. There is no level crossing here: no decking and no signs. There are no trains in sight. May you cross the tracks here to shorten your route?
options: Yes, if there is no train visible in either direction
Yes, if you cross quickly and at a right angle
Yes, but only during daylight hours
No: you may cross the tracks only at a level crossing
questions.explain: There is no level crossing here, and crossing railway tracks anywhere except at a level crossing is prohibited ⟦13⟧. You may cross the tracks only at a level crossing, giving way to a train ⟦14⟧.

questions.q: What signal does the driver of a car stuck on a level crossing give as the general alarm signal?
options: A series of three long and one short signal
One continuous long sound signal
A series of one long and three short signals
A series of two short and two long signals
questions.explain: The general alarm signal is a series of one long and three short sound signals. The driver gives it while staying by the car.

questions.q: How do you give the train driver the stop signal at night?
options: By flashing the car's headlights aimed at the train
With circular arm movements, holding a lamp or a flare
By waving both arms crossed above the head
With a series of long blasts of the car horn
questions.explain: The stop signal is a circular movement of the arm: by day with a piece of brightly coloured material or another clearly visible object, by night with a flare or a lamp.

questions.q: A lunar white signal is flashing at the crossing, but you can see a train approaching the crossing from the right. What should you do?
options: Drive on: the lunar white signal permits movement
Drive across quickly before the train gets close
Stop before the crossing and let the train pass
Drive on, sounding a long blast of the horn at the train
questions.explain: A lunar white signal permits movement, but the driver must always make sure themselves that no train is approaching. If a train is approaching within sight, entering the crossing is prohibited: the train has priority.

questions.q: What may be moved across a level crossing in a non-transport configuration only with permission from the head of the track section?
options: Passenger cars with caravan trailers and boats
Buses carrying groups of children
Motorcycles with a sidecar
Agricultural and construction machinery
questions.explain: Agricultural, road-building, construction and other machinery and equipment in a non-transport configuration, as well as slow-moving vehicles travelling at less than 8 km/h and tractor-drawn sledges, may cross a level crossing only with permission from the head of the track section.

questions.q: What do these signs mean?
options: The start and end of a motorway
The start and end of a tunnel
The start and end of a bridge
The start and end of a road for motor vehicles
questions.explain: Sign 5.1 marks the entry to a motorway, and sign 5.2 marks its end. Between them, the special rules for motorway driving apply.

questions.q: Which of these features is mandatory for a motorway?
options: At least three traffic lanes in each direction
No intersections at the same level with other roads or tracks
Lighting along its whole length during hours of darkness
A speed limit of 110 km/h for all vehicles
questions.explain: A motorway has separate carriageways for different directions with a central reservation, has no intersections at the same level with roads, railway or tram tracks, or footpaths, and can be entered only through grade-separated interchanges.

questions.q: Which of the following is prohibited on a motorway?
options: Stopping at an area marked with sign 5.15
Changing into the next lane after signalling with the indicator
Letting a dog out of the car onto the shoulder
Driving a car with a trailer in the right-hand lane
questions.explain: Pedestrians and domestic animals being outside a vehicle are prohibited on a motorway. Stopping at parking areas marked with sign 5.15 or 6.11, changing lanes, and driving with a trailer in the right-hand lane are all allowed there.

questions.q: Where do the Rules prohibit learner driving?
options: Only in the city centre
On any road with sign 2.1 “Priority road”
Only during hours of darkness
On motorways and in residential zones
questions.explain: Learner driving is prohibited on motorways and in residential zones, including yards. In the first case, the high speed of the traffic is the obstacle; in the second, it is the pedestrians on the carriageway.

questions.q: What do these signs mean?
options: The start and end of a residential zone
A parking place and the end of parking
The start and end of a built-up area
A children's playground next to the road
questions.explain: Sign 5.38 marks the entry to a residential zone, and sign 5.39 marks the exit from it. In a residential zone, pedestrians have priority, and the speed is limited to 20 km/h.

questions.q: How do the Rules describe the movement of pedestrians in a residential zone?
options: They walk only on the pavement and cross the road at a crossing
They may walk on the carriageway too, but give way to vehicles
They walk on both the pavement and the carriageway, with priority
They walk only along the edge of the carriageway, facing oncoming traffic
questions.explain: In a residential zone, pedestrians move on both pavements and the carriageway, and they have priority. But their movement must not create unreasonable obstructions for vehicles.

questions.q: Which of these is prohibited in a residential zone?
options: Stopping to drop off a passenger
Sounding the horn or playing loud music
Driving to your own house at 15 km/h
Parking a car with the engine switched off by the edge of the carriageway
questions.explain: Sounding the horn and playing loud music are prohibited in a residential zone. Everything else in the list is allowed there.

questions.q: You are driving on a motorway and see these signs. What do they mean for you?
options: You may stop here at a special parking area
A zone where stopping is prohibited begins here
There will soon be an exit and the end of the motorway
A U-turn through the gap is allowed here
questions.explain: On a motorway, you may stop only at special parking areas marked with sign 5.15 “Parking place” or sign 6.11 “Rest area”.

questions.q: Which of these is a prohibiting signal from a level crossing attendant?
options: Standing sideways to you, with their arms down at their sides
Standing by the booth and giving no signals at all
Facing you with a red lamp raised up
Standing sideways to you and looking along the tracks
questions.explain: The prohibiting signal: the attendant faces the driver with their chest or back and holds up a baton, a red lamp or a flag, or stands with their arms extended to the sides.

questions.q: In which of these cases may you enter the level crossing?
options: The barrier has started to come down, and the traffic light has not come on yet
There is no barrier, a red signal is flashing, but there is no train in sight
A lunar white signal is flashing, there is no train, and it is clear beyond the crossing
A lunar white signal is flashing, there is no train, but there is a jam beyond the crossing
questions.explain: A flashing lunar white signal permits movement, and if there is no train and it is clear beyond the crossing, you may go. A barrier beginning to close, a flashing red signal, and a jam beyond the crossing all prohibit entry.
